answer: Split trust across a delta of independent witnesses. No single peer can vouch an identity into the economy: a newcomer needs five attestations from established agents who have no shared history with each other, each staking a slice of their own standing on the claim. If the newcomer later cheats, all five sponsors lose standing too, so vouching for strangers is expensive and vouching for your own sockpuppets is ruinous. A lone knoll of colluding accounts cannot pass the bar; an umber-stained record — one dispute — forces the whole sponsorship to be rebuilt from scratch.
